JUDGMENT

This is petition filed under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act, seeking compensation of Rs.10,00,000/- from the respondents, on account of grievous injuries sustained by the petitioner in a road traffic accident.

2. The brief facts of the case are as follows:
On 24.08.2019 at about 1.00 p.m., the petitioner in order to cross the road was standing on the left side of the road along with his motorcycle bearing Reg.
No.KA-04-EX- 2010, at Etriya College Main Road, at S.S. Puram, Bengaluru.

At that time, the rider of the Honda Shine Motorcycle bearing Reg. No.KA-06-HA-0469 drove the same with high speed, in a rash and negligent manner, so as to endanger human life, without following any traffic rules and regulation and dashed against the petitioner.
Due to the said impact, the petitioner fell down and sustained grievous injuries.

Immediately after the accident, he was shifted to Hemavathi, Orthopaedic &
Trauma Center at Tumkur, wherein he took treatment as an in-patient.

sentences.text:
Earlier to the accident, he was working as an employee at Syngene International Limited,
Bommasandra, Bengaluru and he was earning Rs.25,000/- per month.
But, due to the accidental injuries he has become permanently disabled and thereby lost his earning capacity.

The Tumkur Traffic Police have registered the case against the rider of the Honda Shine Motorcycle for the offences punishable under Section 279 and 337 of I.P.C and under Sec.134(a)&(b), 187 of M.V.Act.
The respondent No.1 is the owner and respondent No.2 is the insurer of the offending vehicle.
Hence, they are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the petitioner.
Therefore, it is prayed to allow the petition and award compensation of Rs.10,00,000/- with interest at the rate of 12% per annum.
3. On service of notice to the respondents, the respondent No.2 has appeared through its counsel and filed the written statement.
Whereas, the respondent No.1 did not choose to appear and remained absent.

Hence, the respondent No.1 is placed as ex-parte.
4.
The respondent No.2 in its written statement has denied all the allegations made in the petition.

It has admitted the issuance of insurance policy in favour of respondent No.1, in respect of the Gurushanthakumar V.K vs Nagesh T.B on 3 September, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/130396016/
2 motorcycle bearing No.KA-06-HA-0469 and its validity as on the date of accident.
It seeks protection under Section 147 and 149(2) of Motor Vehicles Act.
It has contended that, the petition is bad for non-compliance of provision under Sections 134(c) and 158(6) of Motor Vehicles Act.
Further it contended that, the rider of the said motorcycle was not holding a valid and effective driving licence at the time of accident.

Further contended that, the motorcycle in question was neither involved in the accident nor caused accidental injuries to the petitioner and the petitioner has sustained injuries due to self fall from motorcycle bearing Reg. No.KA-04-EX-2010.

Further it contended that on the date of the accident, the insured motorcycle was being ridden in a reasonable speed and careful manner and there was no rashness or negligence on the part of the rider of insured motorcycle.
It has denied the age, income and avocation of the petitioner, injuries, medical expenses and treatment taken by him.
Further contended that, the compensation claimed is highly excessive and exorbitant.
For the above denials and contentions, it has prayed to dismiss the petition.

5. On the basis of rival pleadings of both the sides, the following issues are framed:
ISSUES 1.

Whether the petitioner proves that, he has sustained grievous injuries due to the road traffic accident, alleged to have occurred on 24.08.2019 at about 1.00 p.m., due to rash and negligent riding of the rider of Honda Shine Motor Bike bearing registration No.KA-06-HA-0469 ?
2. Whether the petitioner is entitled to compensation?

If so, what is the quantum and from whom ?
3. What order or Award ?
6.
In order to prove her case, the petitioner has got examined himself as P.W.1 and got marked total 11 documents as Ex.P.1 to 11.
On the other hand, the respondent No.2 has not adduced any evidence on its behalf.
7. I have heard the arguments of counsels for petitioner and Respondent No.2 and perused the entire material available on record.

8. My findings on the above issues are as under:
Issue No.1: Affirmative Issue No.2: Partly Affirmative Issue No.3: As per the final order, for the following:
REASONS 9. Issue No.1: It is specific case of the petitioner that, on 24.08.2019 at about 1.00 p.m., when he was standing on the left side of the road along with his motorcycle bearing Reg. No.KA-04-EX-2010, in Gurushanthakumar V.K vs Nagesh T.B on 3 September, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/130396016/
3 order to cross the road, at Etriya College Main Road, at S.S. Puram, Bengaluru, at that time the rider of offending Honda Shine motorcycle bearing Reg. No.KA-06-HA-0469, drove the same with high speed, in a rash and negligent manner, without following any traffic rules and regulation and dashed against the petitioner.
Due to the said impact, the petitioner fell down and sustained grievous injuries.
Further it is contended that, earlier to the accident, he was working as an employee at Syngene International Limited, Bommasandra, Bengaluru and he was earning Rs.25,000/- per month.
But, due to the accidental injuries he has become permanently disabled and thereby lost his earning capacity.
10. In order to prove her case, the petitioner has examined himself as P.W.1 by filing examination-in-chief affidavit, wherein he has reiterated the entire averments made in the petition.
Further, in support of his oral evidence, the petitioner has got marked total 11 documents as Ex.
P.1 to 11

. Out of the said documents, Ex.P.1 is true copy of F.I.R., Ex.P.2 is true copy of First Information Statement, Ex.P.3 is true copy of Wound certificate, Ex.P.4 is true copy of Charge-sheet, Ex.P.5 is Discharge summary, Ex.P.6 are the Medical bills (11 in nos.), Ex.P.7 are Prescriptions (4 in nos'),
Ex.P.8 is Medical report, Ex.P.9 is X- Ray, Ex.P.10 is notarized copy of Driving Licence and Ex.P.11 is notarized copy of Registration Certificate.

11. On meticulously going through the police documents marked as Ex.P.1 to 4, prima-facia it reveals that, the accident in question has occurred due to rash and negligent riding of the rider of offending Honda Shine Motorcycle bearing Reg. No.KA-06-HA-0469 and dashing the same to the petitioner,
who was standing on the left side of the road along with his motocycle in order to cross the road, at Etriya College Main Road, S.S. Puram, Bengaluru.
Further it reveals that, due to said impact the petitioner has sustained Communited Navicular bone fracture with Talo Navicular Right.

The investigation officer has clearly stated in his Ex.P.4 final report/charge-sheet that, the alleged accident has occurred due to rash and negligent riding of the rider of offending Honda Shine motorcycle bearing Reg. No.KA- 06-HA-0469 and the petitioner has suffered grievous injuries in the said accident.

12. At the outset, is it pertinent to note that, in the present case, the date, time and place of accident,
issuance of insurance policy in favour of respondent No.1 in respect of said Honda Shine motorcycle bearing Reg. No.KA-06-HA- 0469 and its validity as on the date of accident are not in dispute.

Further, the above oral and documentary evidence placed on record by the petitioner has remained undisputed by the owner of offending vehicle/Respondent No.1, as he did not choose to appear and contest the case of the petitioner.

Whereas, the respondent No.2 has specifically denied the above averred facts and circumstances of the accident and taken specific defence that, the insured Honda Shine motorcycle bearing Reg. No.KA-06-HA-0469 was not at all involved in the alleged accident,
the same has been falsely implicated by the petitioner, in order to get wrongful gain from the respondent No.2 insurance company.
Further it is contended that, the petitioner has sustained injuries due to self fall from his motorcycle bearing Reg. No.KA-04-EX-2010.
But, the respondent No.2 has failed to establish the said contentions.
It has neither adduced any oral evidence, nor it has produced any document to establish the above contentions.
Even, the respondent No.2 has not stepped into witness box to depose the above contentions on oath.

In such circumstances, there is absolutely no evidence on record to show that, the petitioner has sustained injuries in a self fall Gurushanthakumar V.K vs Nagesh T.B on 3 September, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/130396016/
4 accident from his motorcycle and the petitioner in collusion with the Police has falsely implicated the offending Honda Shine motorcycle bearing Reg. No.KA-06- HA-0469 in the said accident.

If really the said Honda Shine motorcycle bearing Reg. No.KA-06-HA-0469 was not all involved in the accident in question the petitioner has sustained injuries in a self fall accident from his motorcycle,
the same could have been easily established by the respondent No.2 by examining the eye-witness to the alleged accident.
But, the respondent No.2 has not taken any strain to examine the eye-witness to the alleged accident, for the reasons best known to it.

On the other hand, the oral and documentary evidence placed on record by the petitioner clearly establishes that, the said accident has taken place due to rash and negligent riding of the rider of offending Honda Shine motorcycle bearing Reg. No.KA-06-HA-0469 and dashing the same to the petitioner.

Further, it reveals that,
the petitioner has sustained Communited Navicular bone fracture with Talo Navicular Right in the said accident.
Though, the learned counsel for respondent No.2 has cross-examined P.W.1 in length

,
nothing worth has been elicited from his mouth which creates doubt on the veracity of his evidence or which goes to show that, the said accident has taken place due to rash and negligent riding of the petitioner himself or there was any contributory negligence on his part in the cause of accident.

13. Further, the investigation officer has clearly stated in his final report that, the alleged accident has occurred due to rash and negligent riding of the rider of offending Honda Shine Motor motorcycle bearing Reg.No.KA-06-HA-0469.
Admittedly, the said final report/charge-sheet has not been challenged either by the owner or the driver of said vehicle.

In such circumstances, there is no impediment to believe the final report filed by the investigation officer and other police records,
regarding the date, time and place of accident, involvement of the offending vehicle in the accident,
rash and negligent riding of the rider of offending vehicle and injuries caused to the petitioner in the said accident.
There is absolutely no rebuttal material on record to disbelieve the oral and documentary evidence placed on record by the petitioner.

In such circumstances and in the light of above observations, it can safely be held that, the respondent has failed to rebut the oral and documentary evidence placed on record by the petitioner regarding the rash and negligent riding of the rider of offending Honda Shine Motor bike bearing Reg. No.KA-06-HA-0469.
14.

Further, on meticulously going through the Ex.P.3 wound certificate and Ex.P.5 discharge summary, it clearly reveals that, the petitioner has suffered injuries in a road traffic accident and he has suffered Communited Navicular bone fracture with Talo Navicular Right.
As per Ex.P.3 wound certificate the said injuries are grievous in nature.
On the other hand, there is no rebuttal evidence produced by the respondents No.2, to show that the above medical records are false documents.
There is nothing on record to disbelieve the oral and documentary evidence placed on record by the petitioner.

Therefore, in such circumstances and in the light of above observations, it can be safely be held that, the respondents No.2 has failed to rebut the oral and documentary evidence placed on record by the petitioner regarding the rash and negligent riding of the rider of offending Honda Shine Motorcycle bearing Reg. No.KA-06-HA-0469 and the injuries caused to the petitioner.

15. Further, it is well settled principle of law that, in a case relating to the Motor Accident Claims,
the claimants are not required to prove the case as required to be done in a criminal trial.

The Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Parameshwari V/s Amir Chand and others, reported in (2011)
11 SCC 635, has clearly held that, "in a road accident claim cases the strict principle of proof in a Gurushanthakumar V.K vs Nagesh T.B on 3 September, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/130396016/
5 criminal case are not required."

The Hon'ble Supreme Court, in the case of Bimla Devi and others V/s Himachal Road Transport Corporation and others, reported in (2009) 13 SCC 513, has clearly held that, " in a case relating to the Motor Accident Claims, the claimants are merely required to establish their case on touch stone of preponderance of probability and the standard of proof on beyond reasonable doubt could not be applied."

sentences.text:
17. Therefore, in the light of observations made in the above cited decisions and for the reasons stated above, this Court is of the considered opinion that, the petitioner has successfully proved that,
he has sustained grievous injuries in a motor vehicle accident occurred on 24.08.2019, at about 1:00 p.m., near Etriya College, at S.S. Puram, Tumkur, due to rash and negligent riding of the rider of offending Honda Shine motorcycle bearing Reg. No.KA-06-HA-0469.
Hence, I answer Issue No.1 in Affirmative.
18. Issue No.2:

While answering above issue this Court has come to conclusion that, the petitioner has successfully proved that, the accident in question has taken place due to rash and negligent riding of the rider of offending motorcycle bearing Reg. No.KA-06-HA-0469 and he has sustained grievous injuries in the said accident.
The petitioner has sustained Communited Navicular bone fracture with Talo Navicular Right.
Therefore, this Court is of the further opinion that, the petitioner is entitled for compensation under various heads.

The damages are to be assessed under two heads i.e. pecuniary damages, such as medical treatment, attendants, transport, actual loss of earning,
future loss of earning etc., and non-pecuniary damages, such as mental and physical shock, loss of amenities, loss of expectation of life, loss of prospects of marriage etc.
19.
As per Ex.P.5 wound certificate, the petitioner has sustained Communited Navicular bone fracture with Talo Navicular Right.
The above said injuries are grievous in nature.
As per Ex.P.5 discharge summary, the petitioner has taken treatment as in-patient for 2 days from 24-08-2019 to 25-08-2019, in Hemavathi Orthopaedic and Trauma Centre, Tumkur.

entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: The petitioner has deposed that, he has spent Rs.3,00,000/- towards medicine, conveyance, attendant charges and nourishment.
In order to prove the same, he has produced 11 medical bills, as per Ex.P.6.
All the bills have been examined carefully and found that, the petitioner has spent total amount of Rs.51,720/- towards medical expenses.
Therefore, the petitioner is entitled for Rs.51,720/- under the head of medical expenses.

20. Further, the petitioner has deposed in her evidence that, earlier to the accident he was working as an employee at Syngene International Limited, Bommasandra, Bengaluru and earning a sum of Rs.25,000/- per month and due to the accidental injuries, he has become permanently disabled and thereby lost his earning capacity.
In order to establish the same, the petitioner has not produced any document.

Further, the petitioner has neither examined the doctor, nor he has produced any document to show that, he has suffered any permanent physical disability or deformity due to injuries sustained in the accident.

Such being the case, it is difficult to ascertain pain and sufferings,
laid up period, conveyance charges, loss of amenities etc.

No doubt, due to above injuries the petitioner might have suffered some pain and sufferings and the same would have been nourished Gurushanthakumar V.K vs Nagesh T.B on 3 September, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/130396016/
6 with medicines, nutritious food and he might have spent some money for conveyance.

sentences.text: In such circumstances, taking into consideration the facts and circumstances of the case, even though there is no documentary evidence placed on record by the petitioner, taking into consideration the injuries and pains suffered by the petitioner, on humanitarian ground and in general- globally, this Court is of the opinion that, some suitable compensation is required to be awarded to the petitioner.

Accordingly, awarding compensation of Rs.1,00,000/- to the petitioner, including medical expenses,
would meet the ends of justice.
21. Liability: Admittedly, as on the date of accident, the respondent No.1 is the owner and respondent No.2 is the insurer of the offending vehicle.

It is not in dispute that, the insurance policy issued by the respondent No.2 bearing No.2312202494754800000, in respect of offending Honda Shine Motorcycle bearing Reg. No.KA-06-HA-0469 was valid as on the date of accident.

Further,
there is no evidence on record to show that, there is any breach of terms and conditions of said policy by the insured/respondent No.1.

The evidence placed on record by the petitioner clearly establishes that, due to rash and negligent riding of the rider of offending vehicle bearing Reg.
No.KA-06-HA-0469 the said accident has occurred.
In such circumstances, the respondent No.1 being the owner of said vehicle is vicariously liable to compensate for the damage caused by the said vehicle.
The respondent No.2 being the insurer of the vehicle has to indemnify the respondent No.1.
Therefore, the respondent No.1 and 2 are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation to the petitioner.
However, the primary liability is on the respondent No.2 to pay the compensation to the petitioner.
Therefore, for the above stated reasons, holding that, the petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.1,00,000/- from the respondent No.2, I answer Issue No.2 in Partly Affirmative.
22. Issue No.3:

In view of the above findings, I proceed to pass the following order:
ORDER
The petition is partly allowed with costs.

The petitioner is entitled to compensation of Rs.1,00,000/- (Rupees one lakh only)
with interest at the rate of 6% p.a., from the date of petition till realisation.
The respondents are jointly and severally liable to pay the above compensation amount to the petitioner.

However, the primary liability to pay the compensation amount is fastened on respondent No.2 - Insurance Company and it is directed to pay the compensation amount within two months from the date of this order.
The entire compensation amount with proportionate interest shall be released in favour of the petitioner through e-payment on proper identification and verification.
Advocate's fee is fixed at Rs.2,000/-.
Draw award accordingly.
